svg.text: Configuring DPDK on mlx5, with the code: from rte_eal_init to the firmware
The five setup steps a DPDK app runs before its polling loop, one per column. The PMD builds firmware commands itself (DevX); the kernel only checks and forwards them.
each column ends in mlx5_cmd_do / mlx5_cmd_exec(opcode)
the NIC posts a command EQE
the driver writes the input here; the firmware
DMA-reads it and DMA-writes the output
reads the command, checks it, creates or changes the object, then writes the output and status
What now exists in the NIC:
owned by the app; RQ → RDY
DPDK; the rest to the kernel
the code at that layer; indented lines are called from the line above (some steps in between are skipped)

Files: DPDK drivers/net/mlx5/ (linux/mlx5_os.c, mlx5_trigger.c, mlx5_rxq.c, mlx5_devx.c, mlx5_flow*.c) and drivers/common/mlx5/ (mlx5_common.c, mlx5_common_mr.c, mlx5_common_devx.c, mlx5_devx_cmds.c, linux/); rdma-core providers/mlx5/; Linux drivers/infiniband/hw/mlx5/devx.c.
Checked against DPDK main, rdma-core master and Linux master, November 2026. After step 5 the kernel is never called again: the data path is in A day in the life of a DPDK packet.
